forward or create chances with
passes is up to the Key Player.

for the Key Player to try plays

ability. To make the most of that

around the Key Player.

keeping possession, dribbling

passing lanes.

linking short passes. The team as

over dribbling.

building attacks with long passes.

to the front line at once and
create chances.

attacks with one-touch passing.

attacks become fast overall.

strongly pushes the ball forward.

ball vertically rather than
sideways or back.

Counter button.

players up front. The ball goes

balls in front of goal, such as
crosses and corner kicks.

high balls much faster.

making it easier to stop opposing
shots. On penalties too, a correct
read makes a save more likely than
usual.

forward than usual, making it
easier to cover the space behind
the defensive line. Also comes out
faster, for a wide defensive
range.

corner kicks and indirect free
kicks, the GK goes up to the
opposing goal. You do not need to
move the card from the GK
position.

Raises the GK's ability to read
the shot direction on penalties.
More correct reads mean fewer
goals conceded and better odds in
penalty shootouts.

Raises the Key Player's abilities
across the board. Expect a divine
performance while the team style
is active, but beware: stamina
drops quickly.

The Key Player uses plenty of
running to help the team defend
over a wide area. This also eases
the physical burden on teammates.

and approaches opponents
defensively when defending. A
style that shows the Key Player's
presence in both attack and
defense.

On free kicks, if the Key Player
is the kicker, kick accuracy goes
up. When you win a free kick,
activate the team style quickly.

Raises the Key Player's cunning.
Skilled defending gains savvy and
tricks, so even if he commits a
foul, he is less likely to get
carded.

The Key Player's dedication makes
team morale rise more easily while
the team style is active. The
whole team's teamwork also goes up
a little.

The Key Player marks a nearby
opposing player, reducing his
involvement in the match. Even
when your team attacks, the Key
Player stays on his mark.

When defending, the DF line lines
up around the Key Player.
Unaffected by card placement, the
last line sits at the Key Player's
height.

The Key Player starts to overlap.

widens scoring chances. Beware of
stamina drain.

A style often seen in forwards
with a strong defensive mindset.
The Key Player chases the ball
from the front line and lightens
the defenders' load.

When winning a throw-in deep in
the opposing half, the Key Player
takes a long throw. He becomes the
thrower no matter where he is.
